investigator.method:
Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GET (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the venue's own official English-language events listing page and one individual event detail page. The events page is server-rendered static HTML: each of 93 sampled event cards states its own title, a full DD.MM.YYYY date, and an HH:MM local time directly in a `

` block, with a link to the event's own detail page. wp-json/wp/v2/types and a direct probe of the WordPress 'The Events Calendar' REST route were also checked (both still plain, unauthenticated GETs) to confirm no queryable structured-events API exists on this WordPress install — events are static HTML only.

probe_history.reason: The public events listing page (https://badehaus-berlin.com/en/events/) is plain server-rendered HTML exposing 93 event cards, each with its own title, a full DD.MM.YYYY date, an HH:MM local time, and a link to its own detail page. This directly answers the investigation question without needing to escalate: title/date/time/url are all directly present in the static markup. A JSON-LD block is present (Yoast SEO's own schema) but only describes WebPage/BreadcrumbList/WebSite, not Event/MusicEvent; a WordPress 'The Events Calendar' REST route (wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events) returned 404 and wp-json/wp/v2/types lists no custom 'event' post type, confirming events are not exposed via any WordPress events plugin API on this install.

venue_reference: Badehaus Berlin (small live-music venue and 'music salon', Revaler Str. 99, RAW-Gelände, Berlin-Friedrichshain)

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from the retained evidence: the venue's own domain (badehaus-berlin.com), its own <title>/og:site_name 'Badehaus Berlin', and Yoast WebSite schema naming itself 'Badehaus Berlin' at https://badehaus-berlin.com/. Discovered via WebSearch (not treated as authority itself) and independently confirmed by fetching the domain directly.

site_classification.platform: WordPress (wp-content/wp-json present; Yoast SEO plugin present) with a custom-built, non-plugin events listing template — no 'The Events Calendar' or other queryable events REST route exists on this install (confirmed 404).

title.notes:
Each event card's own

...

anchor text, directly linking to the event's own detail page. Sampled representative value from the 'Atlas' card; the same structure repeats identically across all 93 sampled cards.

start_date.notes:
Each event card's own

states a full day-name + DD.MM.YYYY date directly (e.g. 'Wed 02.09.2026 | 19:00 UHR' on the sampled 'Atlas' card) — no combination with page-level or heading context needed; every card carries its own complete date.

time.notes: Each card's own eventinfo line also states an HH:MM local time ('19:00 UHR' on the sampled card) directly, but with no UTC offset or explicit timezone anywhere on the page — a floating local time only, not a confirmed instant. Consistent with this project's v1.2 worked example (example-deterministic-context-ready-01), a floating local time is retained honestly as PARTIAL rather than promoted to a precise PROVEN value.

end.notes: No end date/time is stated anywhere on the event card or the sampled event detail page.

venue_location.notes: Not stated per-event-card or per-detail-page as a discrete field (no address/venue-name block on the sampled detail page beyond generic site branding). This source represents exactly one physical venue (Badehaus Berlin, Revaler Str. 99) — consistent with this project's existing single-venue-per-source precedent (e.g. razzmatazz-barcelona-01), venue identity is intended to resolve via source_id at activation time, not by parsing a per-record field that the source does not actually expose.

source_record_id.notes: No numeric or explicit id is exposed on the card or detail page. Each event's own detail-page URL ('https://badehaus-berlin.com/en/events/{slug}/') uses a WordPress post slug as this source's own stable, canonical path — the same documented judgement already established for LAV (ingestion/lav/discovery.mjs) and moog-barcelona-01. The slug is directly read from the source's own link markup, not inferred.

event_url.notes: Each event card's own <h2><a href=...> and the following 'MORE' link both state the same detail-page URL directly.

price.notes: No price text appears on any sampled event card or on the sampled detail page. Many (not all) cards carry a 'TICKETS' link out to a third-party ticketing provider (Eventim, Eventbrite, tixforgigs.com, vvk.link — different providers per event, not one consistent embedded ticketing widget), where price would presumably be shown, but that is out of scope for this bounded static-HTML sample and genuinely not collected here.

reasons: Identity PROVEN directly from retained evidence.
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML, a resolved supported class, with a CONFIRMED public data path (93 real, current event cards sampled from the live page).
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE, each stated directly and completely on every sampled event card — no context combination needed.
source_record_id PROVEN via a documented URL-slug strategy, matching this project's existing LAV/moog-barcelona-01 precedent.
recommended_family STATIC_EVENT_LIST, an existing named family in this project's collector-family vocabulary.

Decision intentionally stops at READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF, not READY_FOR_ACTIVATION: this investigation retains no DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION evidence item (no collector/parser code or offline fixture reproduction was written in this task), which gate 9 of the activation gates requires. Building and offline-proving the STATIC_EVENT_LIST parser against the retained evidence/events-page.html fixture is separate, explicitly follow-up work.
